findings.title: True protective authority becomes visible when rival supports fail
findings.claim: When wealth, surroundings, and supposed helpers fail, the focus's al-haqq makes God's protective authority perceptible as true rather than newly created.
findings.mechanism: The carrier حَقّ at 18:44:4:2 carries the packet's real-and-firm truth facet; the wider same-surah triggers at 18:17 and 18:102 deny a rightly guiding protector for the astray and expose the futility of taking rival protectors, returning that denial through the focus's authority claim.
findings.reader_payoff: The collapse in the surrounding argument becomes an exposure of causal exclusivity: what was true before the collapse is seen when substitutes can no longer carry the claim.
findings.containment: This is a contextual resonance of root_000347/B001 with divine walayah; it does not activate the other haqq branches or make the wider ayat replace the focus's ordinary truth qualification.

epistemic.reason: A trusted anchored publication supplies the candidate relation, while the additional walk and connection evidence are legacy or review nominations; the exact carrier and target ayah surfaces are supplied, so the relation is retained with provenance qualification.

findings.reader_payoff: Reward and outcome no longer sit as two unrelated superlatives: the reader can see the end as the condition that remains after the intervening sequence has run its course.
findings.containment: The ordinary positive final-result reading remains intact. This does not reduce uqba to succession alone, turn the wider parallels into a grammar decision, or activate every branch of ع ق ب.

findings.reader_payoff: The repetition of better becomes an active measuring instrument: the reader can see the focus reassigning comparison away from the owner's visible advantage and toward divine evaluation of reward and end.
findings.containment: This activates the comparative-choice facet of root_000452/B003 as a qualified contextual resonance. It does not decide a single syntactic attachment for al-haqq or claim that khayr means material wealth in the focus.
